title: New comments attribute the lost write to a 'state-prop failure'/state-view divergence that does not reproduce in the pinned google-adk==2.2.0; the real trigger is the output_key write-skip (which the PR's reachability claim correctly cites)
evidence: agent.py:587-589: 'so a DIRTY review from an earlier attempt can survive a state-prop failure on a clean final attempt and reach finalize as a non-None dirty value.' test_gate_state_marshalling.py:63-65: '``ctx.state`` is a ``State`` built on a stale snapshot (separate from the live dict), so ``ctx.state.get(<child output_key>)`` returns ``None`` exactly as it does in production one call after ``run_node``.' EMPIRICAL: a full Workflow->NodeRunner harness on the pinned google-adk==2.2.0 (venv) shows the parent's ctx.state.get(<child output_key>) returns the child's write one call after run_node (Context._state wraps invocation_context.session.state — the live dict — and append_event mutates it in place via session.state.update). The write-skip trigger IS real and verified: LlmAgent._save_output returns without writing when the final response has no text part or an empty final chunk (.venv/.../llm_agent.py:940-949), documented at pii_reviewer.py:248 (tool-call-only) and anonymizer.py:313 (schema-fail); after_agent_callback fires every turn (base_agent.py:311/359), so the stamp-lands-while-write-lost window holds.
detail: The reachability claim's substance is confirmed (ADK skips output_key writes; stamp always fires), but the 'state-view snapshot divergence' framing carried into this PR's new comments is not reproducible in the pinned ADK — mechanism framing only; the fix and both tests are unaffected (negative control empirically verified to bite via the run_node fake's direct no-write).
recommended_fix: Correct the new inline comments and the _DivergentCtx docstring to name the real mechanism (output_key write-skip, llm_agent.py:940-949) instead of the state-view divergence; no code change required.
